lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Launch and diagnostic: theorems about lines and angles

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Read the example first. You are not expected to know this yet.

items.prompt: Parallel lines, transversal, one angle 70°. Alternate interior angle?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Try each one. If you get stuck, write what you do know and move on.

items.prompt: In a triangle, the two remote interior angles measure 46° and 28°. Find the exterior angle at the third vertex.
In a parallelogram, one angle measures 52°. Find the consecutive angle.
In a triangle, a segment joins the midpoints of two sides. The third side measures 50. Find the length of the midsegment and state its relationship to the third side.
choices: 25, and it is parallel to the third side
50, and it is parallel to the third side
100, and it is parallel to the third side
25, and it is perpendicular to the third side

items.prompt: A proof concludes that vertical angles are congruent. Which statement supplies the missing justification?
choices: Vertical angles are congruent by definition.
Each vertical angle is supplementary to the same adjacent angle, so both have the same measure.
The two lines are parallel, forcing the angles to match.
The angles are congruent because they are opposite in position.

items.prompt: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle measures 42°. Find the measure of the corresponding angle.

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Show what you can do so far. This sets the starting point, not a grade.

items.prompt: In a triangle, the two remote interior angles measure 27° and 60°. Find the exterior angle at the third vertex.
In a parallelogram, one angle measures 71°. Find the opposite angle.
